summary: ODYSSEY is a web app that helps teams rehearse Moon and Mars missions on Earth. You describe a mission in plain English. An AI agent splits it into experiments, sets measurable requirements, and ranks 39 curated Earth analog sites for each experiment using open NASA data (LRO LOLA and Diviner, MOLA, NASA POWER, MODIS). Each site is compared with the lunar south pole or Jezero crater on 31 conditions, and the app shows exactly where Earth stops being a good stand-in. Gaps are never hidden: each is labelled as a dataset to connect, a field measurement to make, or physics Earth cannot provide, such as gravity or vacuum, with a proposed chamber test instead. It ends with a multi-site field campaign and a report. Analog sites are usually picked by reputation. ODYSSEY makes that choice traceable, per experiment, with every number tied to a source or a stated assumption.
details:
What it does

ODYSSEY turns a Moon or Mars mission brief into a field-testing plan on Earth. A user types a mission in plain English, for example "a seven-day lunar expedition with geological sampling, rover navigation, equipment deployment, thermal survival and dust mitigation".

How it works

1. Define. An AI agent maps the brief to experiments and quotes the words that justify each one. Each experiment gets measurable requirements, such as maximum slope or temperature range, each labelled as stated in the brief or as an assumption.

2. Discover. 39 curated Earth analog sites are checked against hard limits, then ranked separately for every experiment on terrain, temperature, geology, access and evidence. A global screen of 81,575 land cells found 80 more candidate regions. A "planetary twin" view puts each site beside the target (the lunar south pole or Jezero crater on Mars) on 31 conditions. Values are compared only when the quantity and scale match, so air temperature is never compared with surface temperature.

3. Validate. "Challenge this match" shows how a high similarity score drops once hard limits and missing evidence are checked; in the demo, 92 becomes 76. Every gap is named: a dataset not yet connected, a field measurement needed (with the standard test), or physics Earth cannot provide, such as gravity, vacuum or the lunar night. Sources the agent finds online stay unverified until the quoted value is found word for word in the full document.

4. Rehearse. For conditions no site offers, it proposes controlled tests, such as a thermal-vacuum chamber or gravity offload, in numbered steps labelled as proposals, not results. An optimiser then builds a multi-site campaign three ways: best science, least travel, fewest facilities. A report exports as Markdown or JSON.

Benefits and impact

Analog sites are often chosen by reputation. ODYSSEY makes the choice traceable and specific to each experiment: which site suits which test, why, and what must still be tested elsewhere. This can save mission teams field time and money and avoid false confidence in an analog. Students and the public can also see why a desert is or is not a good stand-in for the Moon or Mars.

What makes it creative

- It ranks sites per experiment, not per planet.

- It treats Earth's shortfalls as results, not failures, and offers a next step for each.

- It explains its reasoning visually:

- a similarity score broken into its weighted parts;

- Earth and the target side by side;

- log-scale pressure and gravity comparisons;

- sun-angle and crater-shadow diagrams for polar light;

- dust-flight arcs under each planet's gravity;

- relationships between measured conditions across sites.

- While the agent runs, Moon or Mars and Earth are scanned together in 3D. When the first sites are ranked, the view hands off to the best one.

Tools and technologies

- Code: TypeScript, React 19, Three.js and Vite for the interface; Node.js 22 with SQLite and live server-sent events for the backend.

- Data pipelines: Python (rasterio, STAC, H3).

- AI: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through the OpenCode API for the agent. Every number comes from tested code, and the app also runs fully without the AI.

- Deployment and tests: Docker and Azure Container Apps; 71 automated tests.

- Data: NASA (LRO LOLA and Diviner, MGS MOLA, NASA POWER, MODIS, GIBS, NSSDC), ESA Copernicus (DEM, Sentinel-2, WorldCover), CSA RADARSAT-1 and Macrostrat.

What we considered

- Scientific honesty: missing data is never counted as a match, and fabricated precision is never shown.

- Traceable claims: every value links to its source, resolution and date.

- Clarity for non-experts: plain language and visual explanations.

- Accessibility: works on phones, supports reduced motion, and an open-source code base (Apache-2.0) others can extend.

Limits

This is a prototype:

- 39 curated sites and two targets.

- Reanalysis climate at about 50 km resolution and 40 m terrain.

- Several requirement thresholds are assumptions, and they're labelled as such.

- Simulation outputs are first-order models, not facility results.

Links: live app https://odyssey.qd.je · code https://github.com/MahmoudAdelbghany/ODYSSEY
